description: Agent Cybersecurity: submit a service’s exported configuration with its declared configuration: the declaration with each port it lists with its protocol and service, the TLS minimum, the networks administrative surfaces may be reached from (public, internal, VPN or localhost) and its text; the export with the day it was taken, each listening port with its protocol, service and exposure, the TLS minimum version enabled, the weak ciphers enabled and the day the certificate expires, each default credential with the system and whether it was changed, and each administrative surface with its name, exposure and whether it asks a second factor; and optionally the day the record is read on. The signed report gives the declaration, the export, the undeclared public and internal ports and the declared ports absent from the export, the TLS minimum on each side with whether the export meets it, the weak ciphers and the certificate’s days left, the default credentials unchanged, and the administrative surfaces exposed or without a second factor, and counts them, and names an exposed configuration: a public port the declaration does not list, a TLS minimum below the declared one, a default credential unchanged, an administrative surface reachable from outside the allowed networks and an expired certificate; then an undeclared internal port, a declared port absent from the export, weak ciphers, a certificate expiring inside 30 days and an administrative surface with no second factor, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No declared ports, no listeners in the export, no TLS minimum on both sides, no record of default credentials or administrative surfaces, or an undeclared listener with no exposure leaves the configuration unverified. TLS versions are read as written, so 1.2, TLS 1.2 and TLSv1.2 are one. This reads the exported configuration itself: wever_firewall-order-check reads a payment firewall’s design, where its checks run against settlement and which order paths bypass its cap, not a service’s exported configuration, and wever_sandbox-isolation-check reads a test environment’s credentials, reach and data for paths into production, not the ports, TLS and surfaces a service exposes. Verdict cyber_config_exposed, cyber_config_partial, cyber_config_unverified or cyber_config_hardened. POST /api/cyber-config-check. Reads the security records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment, system scan, probe or external write. Agent Cybersecurity reads an organization’s own security records after the fact and checks them against the stated policy and against themselves: standing access, the secrets inventory, the component and patch record, the exported configuration, logging coverage, backup and restore evidence, a vendor’s security evidence and incident readiness. Beside it, the Agent Risk checks such as wever_risk-exposure-check read one planned action’s worst case and limits before it runs, while a cyber check reads security posture from the records; and the security reads elsewhere in the catalog keep their families, each named beside the check it meets. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-cybersecurity-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-cybersecurity/.

as_of.description: The day the records are read on, such as 2026-11-02.

admin_exposure.description: Where administrative surfaces may be reached.

mfa.description: Whether it requires a second factor.

default_credentials.description: Each default credential, with whether it was changed.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.
